title: Fragile single-cone Dirac quantum walks in two dimensions
authors: C. W. J. Beenakker, J. Sánchez Férnan, J. Tworzydło
abstract: It is known that a one-dimensional (1D) quantum walk gives a local space-time discretization of the massless Dirac equation with a single quasi-energy cone (no fermion doubling at low energies), keeping the fundamental symmetries (chiral and time-reversal) of the continuum theory. We show that the analogous 2D construction is fundamentally more fragile. Local two-band quantum walks can have an unpaired Dirac cone, but the protecting symmetries then cease to be ordinary on-site symmetries: they become non-symmorphic, involving half-lattice translations, and are broken by generic spatial inhomogeneities. In particular, we demonstrate that the 2D Dirac quantum walk based on the Ho-Chalker network model can be gapped by potential scattering.
summary: This paper demonstrates that while 1D quantum walks can mimic gapless Dirac physics with preserved symmetries, their 2D counterparts are fundamentally unstable. The authors prove that generic potential scattering terms break the necessary protecting symmetries, leading to the opening of a gap at zero energy for the Dirac cone.
main_problem: The study investigates whether a two-dimensional (2D) Dirac quantum walk, analogous to continuum physics models like graphene, retains topological protection against gapping induced by potential scattering or disorder.
main_result: Unlike the 1D case, the 2D Dirac quantum walk is fundamentally fragile; its unpaired $\epsilon=0$ cone can be gapped by generic spatial inhomogeneities or potentials due to symmetry constraints imposed by locality.
method: The authors analyze the system using Floquet theory and examine the symmetries (chiral and time-reversal) of the lattice Hamiltonian. They employ mathematical tools involving Laurent polynomials to constrain the existence of gapless points.
model_or_system: The model is a local two-band quantum walk implemented on a $(2+1)$-dimensional space-time lattice, whose continuum limit approximates the massless Dirac equation. Specific realizations include Palindromic, Squared, and Ho-Chalker quantum walks.
key_observables: Quasi-energies ($\epsilon_n$), gap size ($\Delta$) at $\epsilon=0$, and the preservation/breaking of chiral and time-reversal symmetries.
important_parameters: The strength and periodicity ($\mathbf{Q}$) of applied potentials ($V$ or $M$), which act as disorder terms.
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily focuses on local, two-band spin-1/2 implementations and assumes the potential scattering is short-range correlated.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the momentum dependence of quasi-energies showing gap opening for various potentials (e.g., staggered potentials), confirming the gapping effect on the Dirac cone.
paper_structure: The paper contrasts the robust 1D case with the fragile 2D case, demonstrating symmetry breakdown under disorder. It systematically tests different quantum walk constructions (Palindromic, Ho-Chalker) against specific potential scattering terms to prove gap opening.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous lattice model framework for understanding how topological protection, robust in continuum models, breaks down when discretized into higher dimensions due to the constraints of locality and symmetry on the underlying quantum walk operator.
